international.title: Shabana Mahmood pledges to tackle ‘corrosive and growing perception of two-tier policing’ – UK politics live
international.summary: Home secretary to give speech to National Police Chiefs’ Council addressing concerns that officers treats groups differently Good morning. Shabana Mahmood has done two of the most difficult jobs in the government. With Labour under pressure from anti-migrant populists, in Reform UK, in the Conservative party and in the media, as justice secretary and home secretary she has been on the frontline in all the debates where the fight between the right and progressive politics has been most intensive. And she has developed a bold, novel, and largely successful strategy for winning these battles; she disarms her critics by agreeing with them. Not entirely, of course. She is still a Labour cabinet minister. But sometimes she can sound a bit like Chris Philp. This is about fairness, Ed, and it’s a very important point. When I talk about two-tier policing, I’m talking about the way that different groups of marchers are treated. For instance, if you go to a Pride march, there are police with rainbow flags on their cars. During the Black Lives Matter protests, the police took the knee. But you go to these protests, and do you see the police waving swastikas? No you don’t. When was the last time you saw a film of a policeman kicking a brown-skinned person in the head? Well, OK , but when was the last time you saw a video of a policeman trying to set fire to a building full of refugees? Exactly. That’s what we mean by two-tier policing. We must tackle head-on the corrosive and growing perception of two-tier policing in this country. Now let me be clear: I know the vast majority of officers police impartially and that policing without fear or favour is their creed. Mahmood will lament the low levels of black officers in police forces, while also warning against “misguided attempts at course correction” that lead to “differential treatment”. And she will warn officers against engaging with “activist groups”, telling them to “leave the politics to the politicians”. We must also be wary of misguided attempts at course correction, where the pursuit of equality leads instead to differential treatment. To the public, it was patently absurd to tell police officers that fair policing does not mean treating everyone the same. Continue reading...
